blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Make the representative dense run performant, make all upgrade choices visually authored and numerically truthful, and guarantee clean failure/victory teardown into Title and replay while preserving the verified movement, combat, shell, result-snapshot, enemy-role, and native Godot baselines.

diagnosis.root_cause: Three independent release blockers remain: enemy separation performs an O(n²) roster scan from every actor; upgrade presentation duplicates vague static claims instead of projecting the authoritative modifier data used by application; and Return-to-Title relies on deferred boss deletion without a synchronous, observable run-actor retirement invariant.

stop_conditions: Do not expand implementation into deferred camera, pause, animation, audio-semantic, primitive-presentation, VFX, or result-input issues.
Do not replace preserved assets or alter the verified movement, dash, enemy-role, result-statistics, shell-navigation, accessibility-setting, or UI-scale behavior.

Stop the dense-steering optimization if it compromises deterministic targeting, telegraph escape lanes, exactly-once death/drop behavior, or pool-generation isolation; correct that regression before continuing.
Do not claim issue or gap closure from Developer self-validation; formal recapture, performance judgment, and closure remain with GameLoop Runtime and Tester.
The iteration is implementation-complete only when all three task acceptance sets pass focused self-validation and both native project and host boot baselines remain clean.

strategy.rationale: Treat each selected issue as a separate root-cause family: centralize bounded crowd-neighbor work, derive upgrade copy and application from one authoritative projection, and establish an idempotent run teardown barrier. This advances the selected dense-performance increment while giving Tester direct black-box and white-box closure paths for all three active issues.

code: Run the frozen native_godot_project and host_godot_boot checks; reject fatal import, resource, GDScript, recurring runtime, freed-instance, or signal errors.
Inspect the dense-steering call graph and telemetry to confirm EnemyActor no longer performs full-roster work and every registry lifecycle edge is handled.
Inspect all twelve upgrade definitions to confirm display projection and application share authoritative modifier rules and every runtime card binds a real icon.
Inspect every Result, Title, Retry, and fresh-start path to confirm it enters the same idempotent teardown barrier.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester profiles a representative 1920×1080 final wave with 25–40 ordinary enemies, the Bellkeeper, all three weapon families, pickups, UI, animation, VFX, lights, and audio, then repeats three complete retries and compares frame-time distribution and lifecycle counters.

Tester opens legal drafts for focused bolt, close sweep, and orbiting area-control paths; capture pre-choice card/runtime state, choose once with ordinary input, capture post-choice authoritative state, and observe the next relevant combat event.

Tester executes ordinary failure and victory routes through Result→Title→Play, pairing first-Title and new-run screenshots with teardown receipt, boss/group/spawner state, pause state, audio ownership, terminal snapshot, and clean logs.

Tester retains the fixed smoke patrol for boot/title/play, movement/dash, camera, automatic targeting and attack, enemy lifecycle/drop, collection/draft, player damage, pause/resume, audio ownership, Result, Retry, and Return-to-Title.
visual: Capture dense Wave 4/final-wave gameplay from the shipped camera and confirm crowd spacing, actors, telegraphs, escape lanes, pickups, and weapon effects remain readable after steering optimization.

Capture representative Lantern, Gravespade, and Wandering Wisps three-card drafts at 1920×1080 and 100% UI scale; verify semantic icons, exact values, focus state, alpha edges, native scale, and gothic reference fidelity.
Capture the first observable Title frame after both failure and victory; no Bellkeeper, hostile telegraph, attack effect, stale boss HUD, or run-owned presentation may remain behind the shell.

done_when: EnemyActor physics and steering contain no per-actor full-tree or full-active-roster scan; one encounter-owned registry refresh or an equivalently bounded staggered cache supplies local candidates.

At 36 active ordinary enemies, candidate telemetry reports at most one registry rebuild per physics frame, at most one neighbor query per approaching actor, and no more than 12 candidate comparisons per actor (432 total at 36), with active count, rebuild count, query count, candidate visits, and maximum query size exposed in the encounter snapshot.
Wave-4 and final-wave play preserve role-specific approach motion, separation, recoverable lanes, attack telegraphs, deterministic targeting, and exactly-once hurt/death/drop behavior.
Activate, defeat, pool-return, reactivate, Retry, and two further Retry cycles remove stale registry entries by stable id and generation; live, registered, and pooled counts reconcile on every cycle.

A representative 25–40-enemy final-wave profile is ready for host recapture with the boss, all three weapon families, pickups, UI, animation, VFX, lighting, and audio enabled; no optimization is justified using an empty-arena average.
tasks.instructions: Replace EnemyActor._steer_approach's per-actor get_nodes_in_group("active_enemies") traversal with an EncounterSpawner-owned spatial registry or bounded cached-neighbor service. Register and unregister actors on activation, retirement, death, pool return, stop, reset, and generation reuse. Query only nearby cells/candidates inside the separation radius with deterministic stable-id ordering and a hard 12-candidate budget. Keep the active_enemies group available for unrelated legal-target semantics, but remove it from per-actor steering. Add profile-ready registry/query counters to authoritative encounter state so Tester can distinguish reduced work from reduced density. Do not solve this by shrinking the arena, lowering the required crowd, disabling behaviors, or merely tuning transforms.
tasks.title: Bound dense-crowd neighbor work

done_when: All 12 catalog entries have stable ids, eligibility/rank rules, a bound authored icon, current effect, and a concrete projected result generated from authoritative runtime data.
The same projection used to populate a card is consumed or verified by choice application; the post-choice weapon/health/dash snapshot equals the advertised result before gameplay resumes.
At the current baseline, Focused Flame truthfully shows damage 26→34 and range 11.5→13.0 rather than the contradicted +25% claim; future tuning automatically changes the displayed values.

Representative focused-bolt, sweep, and orbit choices each show every changed stat, apply exactly once under held confirm, and produce the promised next relevant combat behavior without collapsing the three weapon identities.

At 1920×1080 and the preserved 100% UI scale, each three-card draft has readable name, icon, rank, current-to-result values, and keyboard/controller focus treatment with no blank, clipped, matte-edged, or inert card.
Runtime binding inspection confirms the displayed icons are the accepted catalog assets rather than unbound files or title/category aliases.
tasks.instructions: Replace the static duplicated card descriptions with data-driven UpgradeDefinition records and a side-effect-free projection API that computes current and resulting build values through the same WeaponDefinition modifiers and non-weapon rules used by application. Disclose every changed field, including multi-stat rank changes and unlock state, then store those values in offered/selected snapshots for direct comparison. Bind authored gothic upgrade iconography to the actual card controls and add clear focus motion consistent with the reference's dark iron/brass frames and luminous weapon glyphs. Visual family plan: family_id=upgrade_card_icons; prd_style_match=grounded moonlit gothic linework with spectral accents; source_quality_class=final authored UI vector or texture; material_and_texture_evidence=Developer preview plus alpha/edge and native-scale inspection; expected_runtime_uses_or_visible_area_share=three visible icons per draft across twelve catalog semantics; minimum_distinct_source_variants=12; minimum_runtime_variants=12; maximum_single_variant_share=0.0834 across the complete catalog; diversity_axes=weapon family, utility category, silhouette, and accent motif; background_mode=native-transparent vector/RGBA; runtime_evidence_views=first Lantern draft plus representative Gravespade and Wandering Wisps drafts at 1920×1080. Developer owns task-directed asset search/audition and exact source selection; only accepted, runtime-bound icons count.
tasks.title: Make upgrade cards authoritative and truthful

done_when: One idempotent run-teardown routine owns ordinary-enemy stop/reset and Bellkeeper retirement for failure, victory, Retry, Return-to-Title, and defensive fresh-start cleanup.

Before Title becomes visible, the Bellkeeper is synchronously committed inactive, hidden, collision/physics disabled, removed from combat groups, detached from run-owned callbacks and queued for deletion; spawner live count is zero and wave/director activity is idle.

A teardown receipt exposed in candidate runtime state records run serial, route, reason, boss retirement state, active-enemy group count, spawner live/pooled counts, world-active state, pause ownership, and completion generation.

Both failure→Result→Title and victory→Result→Title show no boss, attack, telegraph, pursuit, stale HUD, or run audio on the first observable Title frame while preserving the previously committed terminal result snapshot.
Play after each Title return increments run serial and starts from baseline health, experience, level, weapons, wave, director, boss, spawner, pause, audio, result flag, and UI state.
Three alternating Return-to-Title/Retry cycles leave no growth in Bellkeeper nodes, live actors, callbacks, timers, audio owners, or result transitions.
tasks.instructions: Introduce a single authoritative teardown barrier instead of treating queue_free as the lifecycle contract. Give BellkeeperActor an idempotent retirement operation that immediately terminates behavior, hides presentation and telegraphs, disables collision/physics, removes combat-group membership, cancels run-owned transient work, and emits a final inactive snapshot before deferred deletion. Have RunController invoke the barrier before showing Title or starting/retrying another run, preserve the committed Result snapshot, clear the boss reference only after recording a teardown receipt, and reset encounter, world, wave, pause, HUD, and run-audio ownership in a deterministic order. Keep terminal failure and victory causality exactly once.
tasks.title: Guarantee clean run teardown and replay
